To overcome them, we present an assumption‐based argumentation framework equipped with preferences (p_ABA). It increases the expressive power of ABA by incorporating preferences between sentences into the framework. As a theoretical contribution of this study, we show that prioritized logic programming can be formulated as a specific form of p_ABA.
